2. Plaintiff and one Late Sh. Hans Raj had filed a suit for possession of the property which is part of land measuring about 1 bigha and 4 biswa, forming part of Khasra No.42/2, Village Ziauddinpur,
Brijpuri, Opposite Yamuna Vihar, Wazirabad Road, Delhi against defendant and others and the said suit was numbered as 8976/2016 and was assigned to the court of Ld. ACJ-CCJ-ARC (EAST),
KARKARDOOMA COURT, DELHI.
It is pertinent to mention that initially 03 defendants namely Prabhu Dayal, Kamal Singh Raghav and Chander Pal Raghav were arrayed.

However, vide order dated 16.12.2009, the name of defendant no.2 Kamal Singh Raghav was deleted from the array of parties and in the amended of memo of parties, Chander Pal Singh was shown as defendant no.2.

Thereafter, vide order dated 01.09.2015, the name of plaintiff no.2 was deleted and the suit was permitted to be continued through plaintiff no.1.
3.
For the sake of convenience, parties shall be denoted as they were before Ld. Trial Court.

Appellant herein Sh. Prabhu Dayal shall be referred to as defendant and Sh. Jatan Singh as plaintiff.
4.

The brief facts as disclosed in the plaint are that plaintiff and Late Sh. Hans Raj were the owners and bhumidar in respect of land measuring about 1 bigha and 4 biswa, forming part of Khasra No.42/2, Village Ziauddinpur, Brijpuri, Opposite Yamuna Vihar, Wazirabad Road, Delhi (hereinafter referred to as suit property).
The suit property was previously owned by the father of plaintiff and grandfather of Late Sh. Hans Raj namely Late Sh. Lekh Ram.

Out of the said land,
defendant encroached upon a portion of land measuring 150 sq. yards and made unauthorized construction thereon consisting of three rooms, one kitchen and latrine.
Defendant claimed himself to be owner of the suit property purchased on 31.01.1981 from one Sh. B.K. Sharma.
5. It is further stated that defendant filed a civil suit against plaintiff and Smt. Chando Devi (mother of Late Sh. Hans Raj) but the same was dismissed vide judgment dated 03.05.1997.

Thereafter,

7. Defendant contested the suit on the following grounds:
7.1) Plaintiff had no locus standi to file the present suit for possession as he was neither the owner /
landlord nor had any title or interest in the suit property.

Defendant was the owner / landlord of the suit property for purchasing the same jointly alongwith Sh. Kamal Singh Raghav and Sh. Chander Pal Singh Raghav on 31.01.1981 from Sh. B.K. Khanna, S/o Sh. M.L. Sharma, attorney of Smt.
Chanda Devi, W/o Sh. Gopi.
7.2) Defendant constructed the house on the suit property from his own funds and is in exclusive possession thereof and residing with his family members.

Sh. Kamal Singh Raghav and Sh. Chander Pal Singh Raghav sold their share of the suit property to defendant vide GPA, Agreement to Sell,
Receipt and Will, all dated 27.01.1998.

7.3) The suit of plaintiff was bad for misjoinder and non-joinder of necessary parties as Sh. Kamal Singh Raghav expired and and Sh. Chander Pal Singh Raghav had no right, title or any interest in the suit property having no possession thereof.
7.4) The suit was not assessed properly for the purpose of court fees and jurisdiction.
The value of suit property is more than Rs.10 lakhs and plaintiff had not paid the requisite court fees.

As such,
Ld. Trial Court had no jurisdiction to entertain and try the suit.
7.5) The suit was barred under Section 10 CPC in view of the pendency of R.S.A. 195/2003 case titled Prabhu Dayal Tomar vs. Jatan & Ors. before the Hon'ble High Court.

Trial Court took on record that as a finding to the effect that defendant was not the owner of the suit property, was arrived at by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in RSA No.195/2003, the issue framed that whether defendant was the owner of suit property, for having been decided by judgment dated 21.01.2011 in RSA No.195/2003, was res judicata and no defendant evidence was required or warranted.

After hearing the final arguments, Ld. Trial Court came to the conclusion that the suit of plaintiff deserved to be decreed for the relief claimed in the plaint, deciding all the issues framed in favour of plaintiff and against defendant.

The brief reasons for such findings are mentioned as under:-
14.1) Vide judgment dated 21.01.2011 passed in RSA No.195/2003, it was held that defendant was not the owner of the suit property.

14.2) Plaintiff was able to establish his locus standi and nothing emerged to show that suit was bad for non-joinder and mis-joinder of necessary parties or the suit was improperly valued for the purpose of court fees and jurisdiction.

14.3) The documentary evidence presented by plaintiff in the form of Ex.PW-3/1,

Nothing was brought by defendant to dislodge the evidence presented by plaintiff.

15.1) Ld. Trial Court erred in not giving opportunity to lead evidence to defendant and therefore, the impugned judgment and decree dated 15.11.2019 passed by Ld.

15.3) Ld. Trial Court itself had issued notice to DDA/concerned department while dealing with the application of defendant under Order VII Rule 11 CPC.
During the hearings on the said application, it came on record that the suit property was already acquired in the year 1967.

16.5) The ground taken that Late Smt. Chanda Devi and Late Sh. Hans Raj had not signed the pleadings, accompanying affidavit and vakalatnama & never appeared in the Court is irrelevant.

Based on aforesaid grounds, the points for determination are framed as under:
POINT A: Whether the findings and conclusions drawn by Ld. Trial Court are bad in eyes of law, legally not sustainable and impugned judgment and decree dated 15.11.2019 is liable to be set aside.

POINT B: Whether the suit of plaintiff did not deserve to be decreed in his favour and against defendant for the relief claimed in the plaint ?
18.

Before dealing with the points for determination, a reference is required to be had to some of the dates of relevant orders and events leading to the present appeal, which are mentioned as under :-
18.1) Defendant had filed a suit for injunction bearing CS No.215/1989 against plaintiff Sh. Jatan Singh, S/o Sh. Lekhram and Smt. Channo Devi, W/o Sh. Gopi.
However, the same was dismissed.
The appeal preferred against the said judgment was also dismissed vide judgment dated 28.07.2003.
The second appeal bearing RSA No.195 of 2003 has been dismissed vide judgment dated 21.01.2011 by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.
18.2) Plaintiff and Late Sh. Hans Raj, S/o Sh. Gopi Ram filed suit for possession in 2004 against defendant before the Ld. Trial Court.

After completion of pleading,
issues were framed and trial was proceeded with.

In the meanwhile, the second appeal bearing RSA No.195 of 2003 filed by defendant came to be dismissed vide judgment dated 21.01.2011 by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, holding that defendant failed to prove his right, title or interest in the suit property and was thus not entitled to any relief.

18.3) After dismissal of the second appeal, Ld. Trial Court vide order dated 08.07.2016 deleted the issue no.1 regarding title of the suit property as claimed by defendant for having becoming res judicata in view of the judgment dated 21.01.2011.
18.4) The applications of defendant under Order VII Rule 11 CPC and for review of order dated 08.07.2016 came to be filed.
Ld. Trial Court issued notice of the application to the DDA seeking status of the suit property.

Notice was also issued to the Revenue Department seeking certain information as regard award and compensation qua the suit property and vide orders dated 31.08.2019, the aforesaid applications were dismissed.
18.5) Defendant filed another application under section 151 CPC for taking on record the relevant necessary facts but the same was also dismissed.
Thereafter, vide judgment and decree dated 15.11.2019, the suit of plaintiff was decreed.

POINT A : Whether the findings and conclusions drawn by Ld. Trial Court are bad in eyes of law,
legally not sustainable and impugned judgment and decree dated 15.11.2019 is liable to be set aside ?
20.

Defendant argued that Ld. Trial Court erred in not giving opportunity to lead evidence to defendant and therefore, the impugned judgment and decree dated 15.11.2019 passed by Ld. Trial Court is liable to be quashed/set aside.

Defendant further argued that the procedure adopted by Ld.
Trial Court was contrary to law and against the principle of natural justice and law of equity.

21. On perusal of record, it is transpired that vide order dated 08.07.2016, Ld. Trial Court held that the issue framed to the effect that whether or not defendant was the owner of the suit property had become res judicata after returning of findings to the effect that defendant was not the owner of the suit property in the RSA No.195/2003.
Ld. Trial Court further held that only remaining issues were to be argued and no defendant's evidence was required to be led and fixed the matter for final arguments.

It is pertinent to mention that defendant did not challenge the said order before any superior courts and the review application of defendant under Order XLVII r/w Sections 114 and 151 CPC was also dismissed vide order dated 31.08.2019.
This court is of the view that for the said reasons, the order dated 08.07.2016 became final and binding.

Further, the application of defendant under Order VII Rule 11 CPC was also dismissed for the reason that the plea raised by defendant could be decided while rendering final decision in the suit as a specific issue on the plea raised was already framed.
22. Defendant argued that the procedure adopted by Ld. Trial Court was contrary to law and against the principle of natural justice and law of equity.
This court finds that there was no infirmity in the procedure adopted by Ld. Trial Court as defendant exhausted all possible remedy available to him before the Ld. Trial Court.

Defendant did not furnish any explanation worth name as to why he did not prefer to challenge the aforesaid orders passed by Ld. Trial Court by way of an appeal before the Superior Courts, during trial of the suit.

As the same were not challenged within the prescribed limitation period and even thereafter till passing of the impugned judgment and decree dated 15.11.2019, the said orders attained finality and became binding upon defendant.
23. Defendant argued that Ld. Trial Court should have impleaded the DDA in the array of parties once it came on the record that suit property was already acquired in the year 1967.

In this regard,
this court is of the view that this ground is without any merit as it is well settled that all objections on the ground of non-joinder or mis-joinder of parties must be taken at the earliest possible opportunity and in all cases where issues are settled, at or before such settlement, unless the ground of objection has subsequently arisen, and any such objection not so taken shall be deemed to have been waived.

In the present case, the plea taken by defendant for impleadment of the DDA is not Sh. Prabhu Dayal vs Sh. Jatan Singh (Since Deceased) on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5936931/
9 only beyond pleadings but also not taken at the earliest possible opportunity or even taken before Ld. Trial Court.

sentences.text: 24. Defendant further argued that parents of defendant and Late Sh. Hans Raj had already received the compensation and handed over the possession of the suit property to the DDA and for this reason they were left with no right, title or interest over the suit property.
Further, by not disclosing these facts, defendant and Late Sh. Hans Raj were guilty of suppression of facts.
In this regard, this court is of the view that the pleas raised by defendant at the stage of appeal are sustainable being beyond the pleadings.
The plea that the DDA has already obtained possession of the suit property by way of acquisition proceedings and disbursing compensation to claimants is also found devoid of any merit.

Had this been the case, the suit for possession of the suit property would not have been by filed by plaintiff against defendant who is in possession of the same and asserting his possession,
right, title and interest therein by hotly contesting the suit before the Ld. Trial Court and even by way of present appeal.

25. Defendant further argued that plaintiff concealed and misled the Court as in the earlier suit Late Smt. Chanda had not signed the pleadings, accompanying affidavit and vakalatnama ; in the present case, Late Sh. Hans Raj neither signed the pleadings, supporting affidavit nor vakalatnama but he appeared only as witness, partly cross-examined and later on he expired.

In this regard, this Court is of the view that plea regarding non-signing of pleadings, non-filing of vakaltnama or non- appearance of Late Smt. Chanda Devi in the previous suit is completely irrelevant for deciding the present appeal so is the plea with respect to Late Sh. Hans Raj.

The order dated 01.09.2015 passed by Ld. Trial Court vide which the name of Late Sh. Hans Raj was deleted and order dated 04.02.2020 of this court vide which impleadment of the names of LRs of Late Sh. Hansraj was declined, were never challenged by defendant and the said orders have now become final and binding.
26.

Defendant further argued that Ld. Trial Court erred in not appreciating the contentions of defendant that the plaint was defective as Late Sh. Hans Raj did not sign pleadings, supporting affidavit and vakalatnama.
In this regard, this Court finds no merit in the plea of defendant as the same was never raised before the Ld. Trial Court.
Further, Late Sh. Hans Raj was examined as a witness by plaintiff and even partly cross-examined by defendant.
Defendant further argued that defendant and Late Sh. Hans Raj claimed that they were joint owners of the suit property but in cross-examination, they deposed that partition had already taken place.

On this plea also there is no merit found as the aspect of ownership over the suit property is already settled by the judgment dated 21.01.2011 passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the RSA No. 195 of 2023.

Further, the order dated 31.10.2019, vide which the application of defendant under Section 151 CPC for taking necessary relevant facts was dismissed is also inconsequential for not having been challenged by defendant during the pendency of the suit before Ld. Trial Court and this issue cannot be agitated at this stage.
27.
Defendant further argued that the suit qua Late Sh. Hans Raj was abated after his death.

This Court finds that the argument of defendant in this regard is not only misconceived but also irrelevant for deciding the present appeal as in terms of provision of order XXII Rule 2 CPC as the Sh. opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
16.3) The ground taken that Ld. Trial Court should have impleaded DDA as a necessary party to the suit is also not sustainable in view of the provision under Order I Rule 13 CPC.
In fact, no possession of the suit property was either handed over or taken by DDA.
As such, the plea of defendant is self- contradictory in as much as the suit property is in possession of defendant who even raised construction, during the pendency of the civil proceedings and earning rent / mesne profit unauthorizedly.
Even on merit, the order passed by the Ld. Trial Court on the said application has attained finality for not having been challenged by defendant during the trial of the suit.
There was no occasion for the suit to have been abated.
In this regard,
this court is of the view that this ground is without any merit as it is well settled that all objections on the ground of non-joinder or mis-joinder of parties must be taken at the earliest possible opportunity and in all cases where issues are settled, at or before such settlement, unless the ground of objection has subsequently arisen, and any such objection not so taken shall be deemed to have been waived.
The plea that the DDA has already obtained possession of the suit property by way of acquisition proceedings and disbursing compensation to claimants is also found devoid of any merit.
Had this been the case, the suit for possession of the suit property would not have been by filed by plaintiff against defendant who is in possession of the same and asserting his possession,
right, title and interest therein by hotly contesting the suit before the Ld. Trial Court and even by way of present appeal.
